usage: ndt <command>

  up [what]     bring the whole lab up and verify it
                  ndt up            Ryu + OVS, 128 hosts  (the default plane is OVS)
                  ndt up 4          Ryu + OVS on the P4 test bed's 4-host layout
                  ndt up ovs        the same as a bare 'ndt up'
                  ndt up ovs4       the same as 'ndt up 4'
                  ndt up p4         p4 at the current host count
                  ndt up p4 4       p4 at 4 hosts   (rewrites host_count_override)
                  ndt up p4 128     p4 at 128 hosts
                OVS builds only 128 or 4 -- each is a different ndtwin-lab verb, not a
                parameter. For any other size, name the plane: 'ndt up p4 N'.
                NDT_TOPO=<file> forces a specific kernel model.
  down [--deep] take it all down and prove the machine is clean
                  --deep also kills whatever still holds :8000/:8080/:8081, including
                  processes this stack did not start. Off by default: without it, a
                  stray is reported and left alone rather than killed.
  status [--check]     what is running, who has the lab, and the state that
                decides every number. --check also exits non-zero on anything
                that would make a measurement untrustworthy.
                  it compares the live lab against what the last 'ndt up' asked
                  for, recorded in .test_run/up.target -- data plane kind, host
                  count, kernel graph, and the model file's sha256.
                  exit 0 all compared fields match; 1 one of them does not (the
                  message names it); 3 nothing was compared, because there is
                  no baseline RIGHT NOW -- .test_run/up.target is absent (every
                  ordinary up->down clears it) or unreadable.
                  3 is never "checked and matched", and it is NOT "no 'ndt up'
                  has ever run here": that sentence was taken out of the output
                  on 09-05 (W12/I-1) as false after every teardown, and when
                  .test_run/pids/kernel.exit is there the report says what the
                  last run was.
                  --check also prints a 'residue' row: rules left inside an app's
                  window and locks still held. residue that could not be checked is
                  printed as NOT CHECKED and never as clean. (G-12 / W16-2)
                  residue FOUND is a problem, and it is rc 1 ONLY while there is a
                  baseline: with no up.target the whole report is rc 3, and the
                  residue and knob problems are printed under "everything else this
                  report could still check" rather than raising the code. 'ndt down'
                  clears the baseline, so that is the state at the END of every
                  round -- exactly when a rule is most likely to be left on the wire
                  with no process to attribute it to. Read the residue ROW, not the
                  exit code, when the record row says none. (F2, 2026-09-11)
  clean         just the teardown assertion (exit 1 if anything survived)
  check         telemetry double-count tripwire
  apps [names]  start readers/apps; no args on a terminal = interactive picker
                  energy sim nsr viz te      ('ndt apps stop [names|all]')
                  ndt apps orphans  -- is anything of an app's still running,
                    and is anything of an app's still on the NETWORK?
                    exit 0 neither; 1 untracked PROCESSES are running; 2 a
                    liveness channel could not look; 4 the processes are clean
                    but a rule or a lock is still there; 5 the processes are
                    clean and the residue could NOT BE CHECKED (kernel down, a
                    reading failed, or the plane has no time axis -- every P4
                    fabric). 4 and 5 are new on 09-07 and are deliberately not 1:
                    a live process needs 'ndt apps stop', a leftover rule needs a
                    delete_flow_entry by hand. Every gate that reads this rc has
                    to be updated. (G-12 / W16-1)
                    🔴 THE CODES ARE NOT DISJOINT IN PRACTICE: the PROCESS answer
                    wins whenever it is non-zero, so 2 outranks both 4 and 5 -- and
                    2 is the ordinary answer on this machine, because /proc/<pid>/fd
                    of a root process cannot be read and every app the lab helper
                    starts is root. So "4: a rule or a lock is still there" can be
                    true and unreachable at the same time. The stderr says so when
                    it happens ("and the network is not clean either (residue rc
                    would be 4)"), and the fix for a gate is to read the report:
                    tools/test_workflow/orphans_verdict.sh. (F4, 2026-09-11)
                  stop and orphans also LIST what an app left on the NETWORK --
                    flow rules and held locks -- and delete none of it. suspected
                    by time only: a rule has no owner and its cookie is 0. G-12.
                    on P4 nothing can be dated at all: its flow stats are
                    synthesised and report duration 0/0, so every rule is listed
                    with age=UNKNOWN and none is attributed. (W16-3)
                  ndt apps trim [names|all]  -- bound a running app's log
                    (viz wrote 875 MB in 1h54m; the app keeps running)
  ntg [cli|prompt]     which prompt the topology hands control to
  claim [min] [note]   reserve the lab (default 30m); needs NDT_OWNER set
  release              give it back

  .test_run/pids/ is shared, so 'down' kills whoever is registered there.
  Declare yourself before a long run -- any script can just write .test_run/lab.claim:
      owner=<name>   expires=<unix seconds>   note=<optional>

  WHAT A CLAIM DOES NOT COVER, measured 2026-09-11 (ROLE-4 T4):
    a claim only blocks the 'ndt' verbs. It is not the northbound API and it is not
    a lock. A loop calling /ndt/install_flow_entry and /ndt/delete_flow_entry every
    2 s kept getting http 200 through its own claim's expiry, and kept getting 200
    after another owner had taken the claim; it stopped only when that owner's
    'ndt down' killed the kernel. There is no signal at all when a claim lapses or
    changes hands -- not to the API caller, not to the previous holder. Re-read
    'ndt status'; nothing will tell you.

  On P4, 'ndt up' derives the kernel's topology model from
  p4_proxy/mininet/host_count_override, so model and fabric cannot disagree
  because an environment variable was forgotten -- and since 09-10 the
  two-checkout form of that mistake is refused before anything is built ('sudo
  ndtwin-lab' acts in ONE tree, and 'ndt up' checks it is this one).
  It does NOT make the 4-host-model-against-a-128-host-fabric mistake
  impossible: inside one tree the host count is whatever that file says, 'ndt up
  p4 N' rewrites it, and on 09-05 setting it built exactly that pair (R3-3).
  OVS has no such knob -- there the size is the verb.
